extracted.intended_audience: law students, legal researchers, and practitioners interested in Florida administrative law
extracted.subtask_description: A short research-guide overview of the Florida Administrative Procedure Act (Fla. Stat. Ch. 120), its role in agency rule‑making and decision‑making, and where to find more detailed guidance. Intended to orient readers to procedural protections, publication requirements, and remedies for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Florida Administrative Procedure Act (Fla. Stat. Ch. 120)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fla. Stat. Ch. 120 is the Florida's Administrative Procedure Act. The APA describes the rule-making and decision-making processes for Florida's agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory foundation for administrative procedure in Florida; the guide points readers to the APA as the primary source governing agency procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule-making and decision-making processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA describes the rule-making and decision-making processes for Florida's agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related guide sections (Rule-making; Rule Interpretation and Enforcement) for more detailed discussion of procedural steps, hearings, notices, and internal agency processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements for agency rules and decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA also describes the manner in which agency rules and decisions must be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes publication is a statutory requirement but does not provide the detailed mechanics or timelines; users should consult the linked rule‑making resources or the statute for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge for noncompliance / acting beyond delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency takes action or promulgates a rule in a manner which is not in accordance with the APA, it will have acted outside of the authority delegated to it by the legislature, and its action may be challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This articulates the remedial/contesting principle: procedural noncompliance can render agency action vulnerable to legal challenge; see Rule Interpretation and Enforcement for procedures and standards for bringing such challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pocket Guide to Florida's APA as a resource
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pocket Guide, published by the Florida Legislature's Joint Administrative Procedures Committee and last updated in 2012 (before recent amendments), nonetheless still provides a good overview of the APA processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pocket Guide is recommended as an introductory resource, but users should be aware it predates some amendments and should supplement it with current statutory text and recent guidance.
